observations: Torah #270 is a short two-sentence teaching with zero bechina statements. The entire text is written in eitza (cause-and-effect) mode, describing a chain of spiritual arousal: (1) hitorerrut from another person — seeing a fellow recite bakkashot and selichot with a broken heart causes one to be stirred and begin praying the same way; (2) hitorerrut minnah u-veha — self-generated arousal in which one's own words of supplication trigger a cry of 'vai li', which then triggers a second moment of self-examination ('heikhan ani, umi tzoak kakh') and a still deeper, more personally-owned cry of 'vai li, li davka'. The text does not identify any concept as a bechina of another concept. There is no basis for forming packages — which require at minimum two nodes joined by explicit bechina equivalence — from this Torah. The teaching belongs entirely to the eitza layer of the dataset. No new packages are proposed.
